---
title: "Similarity Network Fusion"
description: "Building one patient similarity network from several data types with SNF."
---

Papers on similarity network fusion (SNF), which combines several data types by
building a patient similarity network for each one and fusing the networks.

## Wang et al. (2014): Similarity network fusion for aggregating data types on a genomic scale

Wang B, Mezlini AM, Demir F, Fiume M, Tu Z, Brudno M, Haibe-Kains B,
Goldenberg A. Similarity network fusion for aggregating data types on a genomic
scale. *Nature Methods* 11(3), 333–337 (2014).

- [doi:10.1038/nmeth.2810](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.2810) (paywalled)
- [PDF in lab-papers](https://github.com/Omnia-Lab-UC/lab-papers/blob/main/wang-2014-similarity-network-fusion.pdf)
  (lab members only)

**Why read it.** The paper that introduces SNF. For each data type it builds a
network whose nodes are patients and whose edge weights say how similar two
patients are in that data type. It then updates each network using the others,
over several iterations: edges that are strong in one or more networks spread
to the rest, and weak edges fade, which removes noise. The networks converge to
a single fused network. The authors fused mRNA expression, DNA methylation, and
miRNA expression for five TCGA cancer cohorts, then clustered the fused network
to find subtypes with different survival.

**Focus on.** The Online Methods, and the Supplementary Note if you need the
full derivation. Work out how the similarity matrix is built from pairwise
distances with a scaled exponential kernel, how the sparse k-nearest-neighbour
matrix differs from the full one, and how the update rule uses both. Each of
these steps has a hyperparameter you'll have to set:

| Hyperparameter | What it controls | Usual range |
|---|---|---|
| *K* | Number of nearest neighbours in the sparse network | 10–30 |
| μ (`alpha` or `sigma` in SNFtool, `mu` in snfpy) | Width of the similarity kernel | 0.3–0.8 |
| *T* | Number of fusion iterations | 10–20 |

The ranges are the ones given in the SNFtool documentation. The fused network
is then clustered with spectral clustering; see
[Spectral Clustering and Embedding](spectral-clustering.qmd).

**Implementations.**

- [SNFtool](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=SNFtool) (R), from the authors'
  lab. It includes `spectralClustering()` and
  `estimateNumberOfClustersGivenGraph()`.
- [snfpy](https://github.com/rmarkello/snfpy) (Python).
